research_question: Can two topologically different five-atom local motifs share one low-entropy core and yield a valid 17/10 four-slope entropy certificate?

literature_overlap.search_result: No source located that reports this exact heterogeneous rooted star/fork conditional-copy screen.
literature_overlap.scope_warning: A web search cannot prove global novelty.

probability_legality.local_generation: Each coloured five-vertex tree is generated by four successive conditional copies along tree edges.
probability_legality.common_core_fact: Every vertex retains the same marginal law U=(X,Y), even though the two whole tree molecules have different joint laws.
probability_legality.rank_one_glue: Couple the two tree molecules conditionally independently over one allowed projection of their selected core atoms; entropy cost is at most M.
probability_legality.rank_two_glue: Couple over the full core atom using X and Y; entropy cost is at most H(U)<=H(X)+H(Y)<=2M.

dimension_gate.reason: Once h determines X-Y at an anchor, adding that full atom contributes at most one further independent dimension.

rank_exactness.consequence: All rank and containment decisions in the finite family agree with rational linear algebra.

conclusion.result: No 17/10 certificate in this deterministic heterogeneous rooted star/fork family.
conclusion.plain_language: Heterogeneity increased the number of recognizable anchors from four to seven, but those anchors still shared directions; the construction remained three independent dimensions short.
conclusion.scope_limit: This is not a no-go theorem for all heterogeneous motifs, all multi-core interfaces, or all entropy inequalities.
conclusion.next_research_constraint: A useful next family must create a new independent direction rather than merely expose more anchors; candidate mechanisms include two separated cores or a non-tree local motif, but each must undergo a new cost and legality gate before computation.
